claim_verdicts.evidence: "optimistic concurrency takes no locks, but arranges for the data modification to fail on save if the data has changed since it was queried. This concurrency failure is reported to the application, which deals with it accordingly"

"Every table has several system columns that are implicitly defined by the system." xmin: "The identity (transaction ID) of the inserting transaction for this row version. (A row version is an individual state of a row; each update of a row creates a new row version for the same logical row.)"

Npgsql docs: "All PostgreSQL tables have a set of implicit and hidden system columns, among which xmin holds the ID of the latest updating transaction... ideal for use as a concurrency token"; sample: uint Version + .Property(b => b.Version).IsRowVersion(). Live api log at stage-2: "UPDATE orders SET status = @p8 WHERE id = @p9 AND xmin = @p10 RETURNING xmin;"

"The concurrency token is loaded and tracked when an entity is queried - just like any other property. Then, when an update or delete operation is performed during SaveChanges, the value of the concurrency token on the database is compared against the original value read by EF Core." + "EF Core has added a condition for Version as well" (UPDATE ... WHERE [PersonId] = @p1 AND [Version] = @p2).

"if a concurrent update occurred, the UPDATE fails to find any matching rows and reports that zero were affected. As a result, EF Core's SaveChanges throws a DbUpdateConcurrencyException". Live log: "DbUpdateConcurrencyException: The database operation was expected to affect 1 row(s), but actually affected 0 row(s)".

Read Committed: "the would-be updater will wait for the first updating transaction to commit or roll back... If the first updater commits, ... it will attempt to apply its operation to the updated version of the row. The search condition of the command (the WHERE clause) is re-evaluated to see if the updated version of the row still matches the search condition."

"all changes in a single call to SaveChanges are applied in a transaction. If any of the changes fail, then the transaction is rolled back and none of the changes are applied". OrderService.cs@stage-2 CancelOrderAsync: order.Cancel(); notifier.Send(order, "order cancelled"); await repository.SaveChangesAsync(); comment "The notification is saved with the order, by the same SaveChangesAsync." Round-1 live run: batch INSERT INTO notifications + UPDATE orders ... AND xmin; 0 new 'order cancelled' rows for order 5.

"Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL." FOR UPDATE: "other transactions that attempt UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT FOR UPDATE ... of these rows will be blocked until the current transaction ends; conversely, SELECT FOR UPDATE will wait for a concurrent transaction that has run any of those commands on the same row, and will then lock and return the updated row". Entities.cs@stage-2 Cancel(): if (Status == "shipped") throw new OrderStatusException(Id, "already-shipped", ...).

Lesson text now equals the round-1 suggested_text and names its condition. EF docs: optimistic concurrency "assumes that concurrency conflicts are relatively rare"; locking makes others "block for the entirety of the transaction", "although note that EF's mechanism throws an exception and forces you to retry instead, which also has an impact". Live api log: order UPDATE carries "AND xmin = @p10 RETURNING xmin" (the one extra condition).

claim_verdicts.evidence: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs@stage-2:45-50: catch (DbUpdateConcurrencyException ex) ... WriteProblemAsync(context, StatusCodes.Status409Conflict, "Order was changed by another request", "reload the order and try again", type: ProblemTypeBase + "concurrent-update", orderId: order?.Id), order from ex.Entries...OfType<Order>(). Live body matches.

Ledger now matches section 2 ("wrap every read and save in a Repeatable Read transaction and retry on `40001`"). PG 17 13.2.2: a Repeatable Read transaction that tries to update a row changed by a concurrent committed transaction is rolled back with "could not serialize access due to concurrent update"; applications "must be prepared to retry" and should "retry the whole transaction from the beginning". 13.4: such failures "will always have the SQLSTATE code 40001 (serialization_failure)".

The token is "compared against the original value read by EF Core"; resolving needs "Refresh the original values of the concurrency token to reflect the current values in the database. Retry...". ConflictResolutionSample.cs: "// Refresh original values to bypass next concurrency check" entry.OriginalValues.SetValues(databaseValues);. So with no refresh the same WHERE fails again; after copying the DB token into the original value the next save passes and writes the tracked status (cancelled) over shipped.
